findings.title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
findings.body: The cache-deletion mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query that supplies cacheUpdatedAt. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper does not refetch that query itself, and its onChanged callback is optional and window-focus refetching is disabled. Consequently, a successful deletion leaves the old cache timestamp and deletion action visible until another refetch or page reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars on successful deletion, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: An empty update does not advance SelectedCalendar.updatedAt
findings.body: Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not update an @updatedAt field: empty updates leave the timestamp unchanged. Thus this new call does not record successful cache refreshes in SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, contrary to its stated purpose. Pass an explicit updatedAt timestamp, or remove the call if this tracking is no longer needed.

findings.title: Use a sed invocation that works on Linux
findings.body: The command uses BSD/macOS syntax, sed -i '', which fails with GNU sed on Linux. When GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in the environment file, the script therefore leaves the previous URL unchanged but still prints that it updated the file successfully. Subsequent webhook subscriptions use the stale tunnel URL. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle GNU and BSD sed separately, and check that the update succeeded.
